name: ラドリオ
address_ja: 東京都千代田区神田神保町1-3
cuisine: The 1949 half-timbered kissaten down an alley off Jimbōchō's book street, dark brown and lit low, chanson on the speakers and paintings that regulars left instead of paying for their coffee. It is where Japan's ウィンナーコーヒー was invented — hot coffee capped with a lid of cold whipped cream — and the food is two dishes: a hard-fried, Tabasco-and-black-pepper Napolitan and a tomato-and-demi-glace chicken curry. About ¥1,000–¥1,999; alcohol all day, with a ¥200 cover if you drink.
neighborhood: Kanda-Jimbōchō 1-chōme — 156 m and 2 minutes from Jimbōchō station exit A7 (Tokyo Metro Hanzōmon, Toei Shinjuku and Toei Mita lines), in the alley near Sanseidō's main store.
gf_detail: For food, no — both dishes are out. The Napolitan is wheat pasta, fried hard in a tomato sauce cut with Tabasco and black pepper. The chicken curry, on the recipe left by the manager who created it in 2004, is built on tomato and demi-glace sauce — a demi-glace is a wheat-flour roux by construction — and Japanese curry roux is flour-thickened anyway. There is no allergen information, no gluten-free item and no substitution. What is fine is the drinking: the coffee, including the wienna coffee, and the whisky and cocktails carry no gluten risk beyond the obvious (skip anything beer- or barley-based). Treat it as a place to have a coffee, not a meal, if you cannot have wheat.
vegan_detail: No. The house drink is defined by dairy — the whole point of the wienna coffee is a lid of cold whipped cream — and both food dishes are animal: a chicken curry, and a Napolitan, which in this idiom carries ham or sausage. Nothing plant-based is listed. Black coffee and the spirits are incidentally vegan, but there is no vegan meal here and no plant milk is advertised.

chef_bio.chef_name: 島崎八郎 (Hachirō Shimazaki) — founder; 臼井愛子 (Aiko Usui) — first mama and inventor of the house wienna coffee
roles: 初代ママ (first mama, 臼井愛子, who also served as vice-chair of the bartenders' association)
店長 (a succession of managers since, changing every few years)
chef_bio.origin: Kanda-Jimbōchō, Chiyoda-ku — the founder's antiquarian bookshop stood nearby from 1939, and he bought the building the café occupies, living on the first floor above it
chef_bio.background: ラドリオ was opened in October 1949 by 島崎八郎, a Tokyo University economics graduate who became a banker, found the salary insufficient, and opened the second-hand bookshop 島崎書店 in front of the Akamon gate at Hongō — selling social science and foreign-language books, and the work of his younger brother, the novelist 島木健作. He opened a Jimbōchō branch in 1939 opposite the Kanda Nikkatsu cinema; the Hongō shop burned in the Tokyo air raids and Jimbōchō became the whole business. Wanting 「本を読みながらコーヒーや酒が飲める場所」 — somewhere you could read with a coffee or a drink — he bought a building near the shop, put a café on the ground floor and his home above it. The name is Spanish for brick, ladrillo; the half-timbering was the fashion of the year it opened, and the bricks are said to be the same as those of Tokyo Station's Marunouchi building and the Ōji mint. Inside is dark brown and low-lit, with a brick counter, wooden chairs of deliberately uneven height, a red sofa and a stove in use since opening. The chanson on the speakers is the taste of the first mama, 臼井愛子, the founder's niece, who also invented the shop's wienna coffee — cold whipped cream floated as a lid over hot coffee, from a regular Tokyo University professor's description of a coffee he had drunk in Vienna, combined with a cream-topped cake she saw while walking in Kanda-Ogawamachi, and the practical need to stop the coffee going cold during long arguments. Usui was vice-chair of the bartenders' association and the cocktails she made are still served; she left in 1996. Artists paid in pictures, which is why the walls carry the work they left, and the cow that appears on the shop's cups, matches and ashtrays was drawn by the sculptor 本郷新. The list of people who used it as an office is a literary map of postwar Tokyo: 伊達得夫 ran the magazine ユリイカ from across the alley and used ラドリオ as his reception room 「毎日三時間くらいは腰をおろしている」; 片岡義男 wrote at the window two-seater every day; 逢坂剛 took the phone call telling him he had won the 1986 Naoki Prize for 『カディスの赤い星』 standing in the shop; 川端康成, 三島由紀夫, 田村隆一, 草野心平, 埴谷雄高 and others passed through. The founder also ran the neighbouring ミロンガ (now ミロンガ・ヌオーバ), and the owner of さぼうる, 鈴木文雄, has said that ラドリオ was his model — 「『ラドリオ』が目標だったから何度も通って勉強した」 — and copied its half-timbering. In 2000 the leaning building was jacked up, its columns replaced and the brick floor raised about ten centimetres. Managers have rotated every few years since; one of them started the monthly ラドリオかわら版, a staff-made newsletter of Jimbōchō trivia still handed out. The room seats 49 (7 at the counter, 42 at tables) and Tabelog rates it 3.71.
chef_bio.philosophy: The founder's original brief, unchanged since 1949: 「本を読みながらコーヒーや酒が飲める場所」 — a place to drink coffee or alcohol while you read.
chef_bio.specialty: ウィンナーコーヒー — the house invention, hot coffee under a lid of cold whipped cream; ナポリタン, noodles cooked firm and fried until the water is driven out, sauced with tomato, Tabasco and black pepper; チキンカレー on the 2004 recipe, mild, tomato and demi-glace based.

anecdotes.text: The wienna coffee was reverse-engineered from hearsay. A regular who was a Tokyo University professor described a coffee with something white on it that he had drunk in Vienna; the mama imagined her way toward it and got the answer from a cream-topped cake she spotted while walking through Kanda-Ogawamachi.
It was also a practical fix — the shop was much bigger in 1949, coffee took a long time to reach the table, and debates ran hot; a cap of whipped cream kept the cup from going cold.
The pictures on the walls are unpaid bills. Artists brought in work and sometimes left it in place of the price of a coffee.
逢坂剛 had been coming since he was a student at Chūō University; in 1986 he was standing in the shop when the call came that 『カディスの赤い星』 had won the Naoki Prize.
伊達得夫 edited ユリイカ from a room so cramped that he used the café as his meeting room: 「ラドリオの椅子に毎日三時間くらいは腰をおろしている。ぼくに向い合っている人は、毎日違うのだ。」

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13006555 lists ラドリオ（LADRIO）under 神保町/喫茶店・バー・カフェ at 東京都千代田区神田神保町1-3, tel 03-3295-4788, coordinates 35.69565/139.75981, 2 minutes and 156 m from Jimbōchō station, 49 seats (7 counter, 42 table), 予約不可, cash only with no cards, electronic money or QR payment, all non-smoking, no service charge but a ¥200 otōshi when alcohol is ordered, hours 11:30–22:30 (L.O. 22:00) Mon/Wed/Thu/Fri and 12:00–19:00 (L.O. 18:30) weekends and holidays, closed Tuesdays, an opening year of 1949, a ¥1,000–¥1,999 band, a 3.71 rating, official accounts on Facebook and instagram.com/ladrio1949, and a note that the seventh manager retired in April 2023. Its PR line reads 「『神保町』三省堂本店近くの路地にある歴史のあるお店。シャンソンが流れるクラシックな装いのカフェバー。」 The Japanese Wikipedia article on ラドリオ, which is heavily footnoted to books and newspaper coverage (川口 2015, 塩沢 2009, 佐藤 2015, 下里 2005/2018, 読売新聞社 2018 and others), supplies the founding history, the Spanish etymology, the half-timbering and brick provenance, the interior description, the invention and purpose of the wienna coffee, the chanson and cocktail inheritance from 臼井愛子, the 本郷新 cow logo, the roll-call of writer regulars, the relationship to ミロンガ・ヌオーバ and さぼうる, the 2000 jacking-up of the building, the ラドリオかわら版 newsletter, the Napolitan and chicken-curry specifications, and the A7-exit access.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Both food items are wheat — a fried Napolitan and a demi-glace-based curry — cooked in one small kitchen. No allergen information is published and no gluten-free option exists.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The house drink is defined by whipped cream, and the two dishes are a chicken curry and a Napolitan. No plant milk or plant-based dish is advertised.

positives.text: Coffee, whisky and the house cocktails are all served all day, so a wheat-avoiding visitor can sit here for hours without going near the kitchen — which, for a shop whose whole point is sitting and reading, is most of the experience.

cultural_comfort.level: Very easy, and worth going even if you only drink coffee
cultural_comfort.note: Two minutes from Jimbōchō exit A7, in an alley near Sanseidō's main store — look for the half-timbered front, since the door is easy to walk past. Forty-nine seats, no reservations, all non-smoking, children welcome. Cash only: no cards, no IC, no QR. There is no service charge, but ordering alcohol brings a ¥200 otōshi. Closed Tuesdays; note the split schedule — Mon/Wed/Thu/Fri run 11:30 to 22:30, but weekends and public holidays close at 19:00. Nobody will hurry you: this has been a place to sit and read since 1949 and people still do. Order the ウィンナーコーヒー at least once — it was invented in this room, and the cold cream lid over hot coffee is the point rather than a garnish. Pick up the ラドリオかわら版, the staff-made monthly sheet of Jimbōchō trivia, on the way out. No English menu, but the drink names are largely katakana and the two food dishes are Napolitan and chicken curry.

enrich_note: Confirmed. A nationwide Tabelog keyword search for ラドリオ (HTTP 200, 44件) returns two restaurants with that exact name — this one, 13006555, and an unrelated ラドリオ in Nagano — and the Tokyo one is at 東京都千代田区神田神保町1-3, filed under 神保町/喫茶店, which matches the light record's 千代田区神田神保町・神保町駅 and its 純喫茶・ナポリタン note. The Napolitan detail is independently corroborated: the Japanese Wikipedia article, footnoted to book and newspaper sources, states that the food menu is built around ナポリタン and チキンカレー and describes the Napolitan's Tabasco-and-black-pepper sauce. Coordinates updated to Tabelog's (35.695648, 139.759808), about 200 m from the sweep's approximate pin. website is left null deliberately: Tabelog lists no homepage, only a Facebook page and instagram.com/ladrio1949, and the X account named in Tabelog's notes belongs to the seventh manager, who retired in April 2023. gf_confidence has been moved down from the light record's 'ask' to 'no' — both dishes on the menu are wheat, and the curry is demi-glace-based, so there is nothing to ask for; the gf_detail explains that the drinks side is nonetheless fine.
